overlap.title: Who were the “sons of God” who took the daughters of men?
overlap.summary: Genesis 6 says the sons of God took wives from the daughters of men and that children were born to them, just before the Lord resolves to destroy man. The passage does not say who the sons of God were.
overlap.reasoning: The passage sets two groups beside each other, the sons of God and the daughters of men, and tells of their marriages and children immediately before God sees that the wickedness of man is great. Nothing earlier in Genesis uses the phrase “sons of God”, and the passage does not explain it. Verse 4 also leaves open how the giants are related to these unions: it says they were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of God came in to the daughters of men, without saying that the giants were the children. In the Hebrew edition quoted, the two words for “sons of God” in Genesis 6:2 are the same two words as in Job 1:6, where the sons of God present themselves before the Lord. Brenton’s Greek has “sons of God” in Genesis 6 and “angels of God” in Job 1:6.
overlap.scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Readers have identified the sons of God as heavenly beings, as men of one family line marrying women of another, or as rulers. Each is an interpretation; the passage states none of them, and this record asserts none. The same Hebrew words in Job show that the phrase is shared; shared wording does not settle what it means in Genesis 6. Jude 1:6 and 2 Peter 2:4 speak of angels that sinned, and are read by some as referring to this passage; neither mentions Genesis 6, marriage or daughters of men. Matthew 22:30 is cited by others against the first reading; it speaks of the resurrection and of angels in heaven and does not mention Genesis 6 either. Check made for an answer elsewhere: the packaged KJV was searched for “sons of God” (11 verses: Genesis 6:2, 6:4; Job 1:6, 2:1, 38:7; John 1:12; Romans 8:14, 8:19; Philippians 2:15; 1 John 3:1, 3:2) and all were read; Matthew 22:30, Jude 1:6–7 and 2 Peter 2:4–5 were read as well. None says who the sons of God of Genesis 6 were. That is a word search, not a reading of the whole Bible, and it does not prove that no passage addresses the question. No G tag is proposed: in Genesis 6:2 and 6:4 Brenton’s Greek agrees with the KJV. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
